subject: gl.tree.nj offered an nj tree different than other software

messages.author: 61b4b7d682b3dc02
messages.subject: gl.tree.nj offered an nj tree different than other software
parts:
Hello all,

I run the gl.tree.nj function by using the gl file and obtained an nj tree. However, when I transfer the gl file into the distance matrix format by using the function gl.dist.pop (gl, method="euclidean") and input into the MEGA software, I got a different nj tree. Some populations were clustered together in one ward in the MEGA output tree instead of separated into several wards in gl.tree.nj output. 

My question is what the data source the gl.tree.nj based on to obtain the tree? Is a different source cause different dendrograms, distance matrix, or alignment? And is there any function could generate the coefficient value between the populations in the dendrogram? 

Thank you!

Best,
Yunjia

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: gl.tree.nj offered an nj tree different than other software
parts:
Hi Yunjia

I am not sure what is going on here. Our script is just a quick and dirty for visualizing your data in one other way. It is a wrapper around

tree <- ape::nj(d)
tree <- ape::root(tree, outgroup)

so you would need to look at the ape package documentation to get to the root of this.

A
